newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Costello says data no cause for complacency.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Costello says data no cause for complacency.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Wednesday there was no cause for complacency on inflation despite data showing inflation remained low in the September quarter.
Costello also told reporters that wage rises should be based on productivity gains, rather than prices.

"They (workers) also know that in relation to wage settlements they don't have to have wage settlements chasing prices; what we can look forward to is wages chasing productivity or facilitating productivity. That ought to be on everybody's minds," he said.
Figures released earlier on Wednesday showed the consumer price index (CPI) rose 0.3 percent in the September quarter for an annual inflation rate of 2.1 percent.
The Treasury's measure of underlying inflation rose 0.5 percent also in the September quarter to stand at 2.4 percent for the year.
Costello said the inflation data were consistent with "a number of pieces of good economic news".
"You never want to get complacent about them," he said.

"Just when we think things are improving we've got to work harder to improve them further and we will work harder to improve them further with better industrial relations, reducing the cost of doing business, a low taxation regime so we can set up long term growth prospects for the Asutralian eocnomy.

"What our government is interested in is long term growth prospects, not for a year or two years, but set up conditions where you can have year on year on the run low inflation growth," Costello said.
He declined to comment directly on interest rates, but echoed the Reserve Bank's previously stated concern about excessive wages growth.
